newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Cash shortage halts work at Russian gold plant.
newsitem.headline: Cash shortage halts work at Russian gold plant.

text.p: A lack of cash to transport spare parts to Russia's large Olimpiadinsk gold processing plant in the eastern Siberian territory of Krasnoyarsk has halted operations, a plant director said on Thursday.
"For us it's an emergency situation," Vladimir Bindyukov, vice-president of the gold "artel", or cooperative, Polyus, which runs the mine, told the RIA Novosti news agency.

The plant, about 3,500 kms east of Moscow, needs to transport 50 tonnes of metal equipment from the neighbouring Kemerovo region to refit its crushing mill but lacks the 300 million roubles needed to move them.
"There has been no money in our bank account for a long time already and people are living without wages," said Bindyukov.
"We haven't been paid for the gold we gave to the Russian finance ministry earlier," he said.

The artels in the remote regions of the Russian Far East and eastern Siberia account for 60 percent of Russian gold production. Output has declined steadily for lack of cash and investment since the demise of the Soviet Union.
Russia's Gold Industry Workers' Union in September forecast Russian gold production at 100-105 tonnes this year, down from 122 tonnes in 1995 and the 1989 peak of 160 tonnes.
